title: Family Law Amendment (A Step Towards a Safer Family Law System) Bill 2020
short_title: Family Law Amendment (A Step Towards a Safer Family Law System) Bill 2020

speeches.speaker: Sharon Claydon
speeches.brief: The speaker argued for removing the presumption of equal shared parental responsibility from the Family Law Act, citing evidence that it leads to unsafe custody arrangements and noting that 40 women were killed by violence in 2020. The bill has support from over 90 organisations, including Women's Legal Services Australia and Rosie Batty's Safety First campaign.

speeches.speaker: Anne Aly
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Family Law Amendment (A Step Towards a Safer Family Law System) Bill 2020, which removes the presumption of equal shared parental responsibility, is vital because the existing provision places children in harm’s way in domestic violence cases and has not been reformed despite numerous inquiries.

speeches.speaker: Julie Owens
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Family Law Amendment (A Step Towards a Safer Family Law System) Bill 2020, which repeals two sections of the Family Law Act that create a presumption of equal shared parental responsibility, arguing it removes the misconception that this means equal time and prioritises child safety amid Family Court delays of up to four years.

speeches.speaker: Tanya Plibersek
speeches.brief: The Family Law Amendment (A Step Towards a Safer Family Law System) Bill 2020 repeals sections 61DA and 65DAA of the Family Law Act to remove the presumption of equal shared parental time, implementing 106 recommendations from three reports on family violence. The speaker also criticised the lack of action on domestic violence reforms and the abolition of the Family Court, citing cases including Hannah Clarke and her children.

speeches.speaker: Clare O'Neil
speeches.brief: The Family Law Amendment (A Step Towards a Safer Family Law System) Bill 2020 would remove sections 61DA and 65DAA of the Family Law Act to end the presumption of equally shared parental responsibility and prevent its misuse by abusive partners, addressing that 70–85% of family law matters involve violence allegations.

speeches.speaker: Terry Young
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Family Law Amendment (A Step Towards a Safer Family Law System) Bill will protect children by prioritising their wellbeing, and noted that the presumption of equal shared parental responsibility under section 61DA of the Family Law Act does not apply in cases of family violence or abuse. The speaker also announced government investments of $13.5 million for family safety risk screening, $10.4 million for co-located child protection and policing officials in family law courts, and over $48.9 million for family advocacy support services through 2022.

speeches.speaker: Anika Wells
speeches.brief: The speech backed the Family Law Amendment (A Step Towards a Safer Family Law System) Bill 2020 to remove the presumption of equal shared parental responsibility, and condemned the Morrison government’s abolition of the specialised Family Court. It cited rising domestic violence demand in Brisbane’s north, including SANDBAG’s 200 police referrals, 80 women on a six-month counselling waitlist, and a 4,018-person walk in Sandgate.

speeches.speaker: Terri Butler
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the presumption of equal shared parental responsibility in family law forces victims of violence to bear the legal burden of rebutting it, and called on the Morrison-Joyce government to remove this presumption, citing support from the Women's Legal Service, the 2009 Time for Action report, a 2018 bipartisan House committee report, and the 2019 Australian Law Reform Commission report.

speeches.speaker: Ged Kearney
speeches.brief: The speaker argued for removing the presumption of equal shared parental responsibility from the Family Law Act to better protect children from domestic violence and coercive control, citing Women’s Legal Services Australia’s recommendation and noting that one woman per week and one man per month are killed by a partner. She also criticised the government’s abolition of the Family Court and its indifference to vulnerable Australians.
